newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zaire-Belgian TV says paras poised to fly to Shaba.
newsitem.headline: Zaire-Belgian TV says paras poised to fly to Shaba.

text.p: Belgian paratroops stationed in Brazzaville, Congo, are poised to fly to Zaire's Shaba province to evacuate Belgians caught up in the civil war there, Belgian RTL-TVI television reported on Thursday.
"We are looking very closely at the situation in Shaba particularly because the fall of Lubumbashi (to rebel forces) seems to us to be imminent," a Belgian officer stationed in Congo told RTL-TVI.

RTL-TVI said around 20 paratroops would fly to Ndola in Zambia on the border with Zaire on Thursday or Friday to prepare the way for the remainder of the 550-strong force should it be needed. The full force could reach Lubumbashi in four hours, RTL-TVI said.
Lubumbashi, in Shaba province, is close to the Zambia border.
A Belgian army spokesman in Brussels said, however, no troops had left for Shaba and they would only go if it proved absolutely necessary.
"We will only go if there is a question of imminent danger, but there's none for the moment," he told Reuters.
He could not confirm the report that an advance group of troops was planning to fly to Ndola.
Belgian Defence Minister Jean-Pol Poncelet left Brussels earlier on Thursday on a weekend visit to the Belgian troops stationed in Congo.
